thread:
tess: Ran the nightly perf sweep on A100 (sm80) and saw a ~25% throughput regression on the causal path for head_dim=30 compared to head_dim=32. stack: flashv3 selected -> fallback to slow path occasionally :thinking:
ryan: yikes. do you have the repro command and profiler output?
tess: here's the exact command I used:
```
./ci/run_perf --model llama-7b --seq_len 512 --head_dim 30 --batch 8 --kernel auto --mode causal
```
perf-bot: job 2026-06-12T03:12:04Z finished. summary: p50=11.9ms p95=17.3ms p999=61.4ms tokens/s=1420
alisa: compare that to head_dim=32 run?
tess: head_dim=32 (same run) -> p50=9.1ms p95=13.6ms p999=45.0ms tokens/s=1880. so big regression on unaligned head.
ryan: looks like the autotuner picks flashv3 for v3-causal when head_dim<32 alignment triggers some non-vectorized path. maybe kv cache layout assumptions? :eyes:
emily: I repro'd locally with nvprof. saw a ton of small kernel launches for sdpa fallback on step 1 for many batches. stacktrace points to flashv3->causal_setup failing heuristic and then invoking sdpa slow path.
tess: uploading trace snippet:
```
[  profiler ] SDPA_FALLBACK reason=headdim_unaligned (30) kernel=sdpa_generic launch_count=1245
[  timing   ] flashv3_try  failed 0.8ms  -> sdpa_generic  p50=10.4ms
```
ryan: hmm. historically we special-cased head_dim % 32 != 0 to avoid v3 because of warp-level loads. maybe v3 autotuner lost that rule when we added seq_len-dependent switching.
alisa: could it be causal vs non-causal branch selection? earlier we saw v3 is much better for non-causal but for causal it needs a different tiling config.
tess: yes, non-causal head_dim=30 runs fine with flashv3. this is only on causal path (kv cache + incremental decode).
emily: repro script attached: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/compare/PR-xxxx
ryan: quick mitigation: force SDPA v2 for causal when head_dim % 16 != 0 and head_dim < 64. that should avoid the fallback thrash. I'll open a small flag PR.
alisa: can we also improve autotuner to record fallback cost and prefer kernels that have stable incremental decode performance? current metric is bulk throughput only.
ryan: good point. autotuner currently probes based on single-batch throughput with full sequence, not incremental decode microbenchmarks. adding a microprobe for incremental decode (mini steps with kv cache) seems useful.
ess: (reaction) :thumbsup:
tess: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/issues/412 with traces and suggested mitigation.
ryan: I'll put up PR to fallback-policy + autotuner microprobe. plan: 1) short-term force sdpa-v2 for unaligned small-head causal (opt-in flag) 2) add incremental decode probe to tuner 3) log fallback reasons to perf logs so we can track.
emily: timeline?
ryan: PR in the next 24h for mitigation, autotuner change in next sprint. will add perf numbers in PR description.
tess: thanks — adding this thread to the incident folder and pinging perf owners. :eyes:
